correctness.rationale: A closed immersion of the six-line cone forces an injective tangent plane and associated-graded map at its vertex. Any singular point of a characteristic-zero normal toric surface has a two-dimensional rational CM local ring with multiplicity embedding dimension minus one (Artin; de Jong p.67). Sally (as recorded by Rossi--Valla p.81) implies the homogeneous ideal of its projectivized tangent-cone curve is generated by quadrics. Each defining quadric would restrict to a conic through all six chosen tangent directions; independent conic evaluation forces every restriction to be zero, hence forces a projective plane into a one-dimensional projectivized tangent cone. The contradiction proves universal nonembedding. Explicit conic evaluation determinant 7 was rerun with exact arithmetic using the included verify.py; it proves nonempty open condition, while the proof handles all target surfaces and configurations in scope. General \\(m\\le5\\) existence follows from a smooth conic and Banks--Coskun--Tucker Example 3.4.

value.rationale: This determines the exact natural minimum number of general concurrent lines obstructing embeddings into every normal toric surface: six, compared with existing universal sufficient \\(m\\ge9\\) and positive construction \\(m\\le5\\). It is a complete sharp generic cutoff, supplies an open rank-test rather than very-general avoidance, and removes projectivity of the target. The proof isolates a structural tangent-cone mechanism, which can inform embeddings into other rational surface singularities; no unsupported consequence for irreducible curves is claimed.
